literal: a fake pipe player fills a seat
meaning_long: faking it among people who really have the skill
source: 《韩非子·内储说上》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
story: Ancient China, the state of Qi. The old king loves the yu, a bamboo mouth organ, and always has three hundred musicians play it together. A man who cannot play at all joins the band anyway: he just puffs his cheeks and wiggles his fingers, and in such a big band nobody notices. He gets paid like everyone else for years. Then the old king dies, and the new young king prefers solos: each musician must play for him alone, one by one. That night the faker climbs over the palace wall and runs away.
continuity: - THE FAKER: skinny man about 40, long face, thin pointy goatee, shifty sideways eyes, sly grin, the only musician in a rust-red robe with a black sash and a small black musician's cap.
- THE YU: a Chinese bamboo mouth organ: a cluster of tall thin bamboo pipes standing in a round wooden base with a short mouthpiece. Every musician holds one.
- THE KINGS: the OLD KING is grey-bearded and kindly; the NEW KING is young, clean-shaven, with sharp curious eyes. Both wear a golden robe and a flat crown with a beaded fringe.
- SETTING: a grand palace music hall with red pillars and a polished floor; the other musicians all wear identical slate-blue robes and are simple, smaller background figures.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

Medium shot in the palace music hall: the faker stands in a row of musicians, cheeks puffed out hugely, holding his yu clearly upside down, eyes darting sideways, sweat drops on his forehead. The musician right next to him (slate-blue robe) has noticed and stares at him, one eyebrow raised. Both faces clear; more musicians blurred behind. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.
Wide shot: the old king sits on his throne smiling blissfully with his eyes closed, listening; in front of him, long rows of musicians in slate-blue robes all play their yu together.
At the palace gate the faker eagerly joins the end of a line of musicians walking in, grinning, holding his yu awkwardly like a broom. (Other musicians only from behind.)

Close-ish shot of the faker in the band: cheeks puffed like a balloon, fingers wiggling over the pipes, eyes squeezed shut as if lost in the music, a little sweat drop. No sound lines needed. (Only the faker in focus.)
The faker happily holds a heavy cloth purse of round bronze coins (plain, no characters) in each hand, grinning widely, in a palace corridor. (Only the faker.)

The new young king sits on the throne, smiling, raising one finger: one at a time. A single musician in a slate-blue robe stands alone in front of him playing. Far behind, at the edge of the hall, the faker peeks from behind a pillar, horrified.
Night: the faker scrambles over the palace wall with a small bundle on his back, legs kicking, panicked face looking back over his shoulder, moonlight. (Only the faker.)
The empty seat (background for the big title)

A single yu lying on its side on the empty polished floor of the music hall in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is a calm, plain hall wall with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing on it (we place the big title there). No people.

A modern meeting room: the same FAKER (long face, pointy goatee, shifty eyes) in a rust-red shirt nods eagerly with a fake confident smile, while two colleagues point at a whiteboard covered only in simple shapes and arrows (no words, no numbers). A few nervous sweat drops show he has no idea. No text, no logos, no screens.
lines: He was in the royal band for years. He never played a note.
The king loved one big band: three hundred players at once.
This man could not play at all, but he joined anyway.
He just puffed his cheeks and moved his fingers.
Nobody noticed, and he got paid every day.
Then a new king came. He liked solos, one by one.
That night, the faker ran away!
A fake player just fills a seat.
It means faking it in a group of experts.
Like nodding in a meeting with no idea what is going on.
title: He was in the king's band for years… and never played a note 🎶 | 滥竽充数
desc: 滥竽充数 (làn yú chōng shù) = faking it to fill a spot among people who really have the skill. Ever done that? 👇
pinned: 滥 fake · 竽 yu (bamboo pipes) · 充 fill · 数 number. 📝 他什么都不会，只是在团队里滥竽充数。(Tā shénme dōu bú huì, zhǐshì zài tuánduì lǐ làn yú chōng shù.) = He can't do anything; he's just filling a spot on the team.
